keyVerseText: And Abram said, Lord GOD, what wilt thou give me, seeing I go childless, and the steward of my house is this Eliezer of Damascus?
rootMeaning: The word אֲדֹנָי (ʼĂdônây) is an emphatic form of the root אָדוֹן (ʼâdôwn), which means lord, master, or owner. This root conveys the idea of firm control and sovereign authority, whether human or divine. The emphatic form underscores the personal and reverential aspect, often translated as "my Lord," highlighting a relationship of submission and respect beyond a mere title. Thus, the root sense enriches the English gloss by emphasizing both authority and intimate lordship.
usageInScripture: The term אֲדֹנָי appears 437 times in Scripture, predominantly translated as "the Lord" (246 occurrences), with other frequent renderings including "O Lord," "Lord," and "my Lord." This consistent use as a divine title, often substituting the sacred name Yahweh in Jewish reverence, reveals its function as a proper name for God, emphasizing His sovereign lordship. The range of translations reflects both the recognition of God's supreme authority and the personal devotion of the speaker.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding אֲדֹנָי as "my Lord" rooted in sovereign mastery deepens our appreciation of God's authority and relational lordship over His people. It reminds believers that God is not only the powerful Creator but also a personal Lord who governs with care and demands reverence. This word encapsulates the biblical truth that faith involves both acknowledging God's ultimate control and submitting to His will in trust. For the Christian, recognizing Jesus Christ as Lord echoes this Hebrew foundation, affirming His divine authority and intimate lordship over the believer's life.
keyVerseReflection: In Genesis 15:2, Abram addresses God as "Lord GOD," expressing his concern about being childless and mentioning his steward Eliezer. The use of אֲדֹנָי here conveys Abram's recognition of God's sovereign authority and personal lordship over his life and future. It highlights Abram's faith posture—turning to the Lord as the master who holds his destiny, even amid uncertainty. This word enriches the verse by underscoring the trust and reverence Abram places in God's faithful lordship.
